risks.risk: Exact model/size/resolution may be different from what the seller claims (and brand confusion exists), which changes value.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the TV’s label/model sticker (back panel) showing brand, exact model number, and screen size; plus a screenshot of the TV’s “About/Device Information” page showing resolution.
risks.if_unproven: Price as a generic large smart TV with unknown exact specs/brand, worst-case for value.

risks.risk: Panel defects not visible in the provided angles (dead pixels, lines, scratches, backlight issues, or burn-in).
risks.proof: A short video clip showing: full-screen solid colors (red/green/blue/white/black), scrolling text, and a close-up of the screen at different brightness levels.
risks.if_unproven: Price as potentially having screen/panel issues (worst-case) until defect checks are shown.

risks.risk: Ports/inputs may be faulty (HDMI/USB/antenna), affecting usability.
risks.proof: A clip demonstrating at least one HDMI input working (e.g., phone screen mirroring or a console/decoder) and one USB playback test.
risks.if_unproven: Price as “unknown functionality” and assume possible input issues.

risks.risk: Remote control may be missing or non-functional; setup may be harder.
risks.proof: Photo of the remote (model number if any) and a quick clip showing navigation on the TV using the remote.
risks.if_unproven: Price as remote not guaranteed (worst-case) until confirmed.

risks.risk: Audio/speaker condition may be poor (distortion, blown speakers) even if the screen is fine.
risks.proof: A clip playing a short video with clear dialogue and volume changes to confirm speaker output.
risks.if_unproven: Price as “audio unverified,” worst-case for usability.

risks.risk: Power supply or overheating issues may exist (TV turns on now but may fail later).
risks.proof: A clip showing the TV running for several minutes (e.g., 10–15 minutes) without shutting down, plus a quick check for any warning icons.

risks.risk: Wall-mount/stand hardware may be missing or incompatible, increasing buyer cost/risk.
risks.proof: Photos of included wall-mount brackets/stand and the mounting holes pattern; confirm what is included in the box.

proof_requests: Clear photo of the TV back label showing brand, exact model number, and screen size (in inches).
Screenshot/photo of the TV’s “About/Device Information” page showing resolution (HD/Full HD/4K) and model.
Video test: full-screen color patterns (red/green/blue/white/black) and a dead-pixel/line check.
Video demonstrating HDMI input working (phone/decoder/console) and one USB playback test.
Photo and quick clip of the remote working (navigation on webOS).
Audio test clip (dialogue + volume up/down) to confirm speakers are healthy.
Clip showing the TV running continuously for 10–15 minutes without shutdown/warnings.
Photos of included stand and/or wall-mount hardware; confirm what exactly comes with the TV.
response.reason: The witness confirms it’s a large webOS smart TV that is on, but the critical details that determine the correct market price (exact brand/model/size/resolution and panel/port/remote condition) are not verifiable from the provided report. Brand/model claims conflict, so proof is needed before pricing.
